chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Ismail son of Abu Abdullah died, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) came to the grave, loosened himself, and sat. Then he said: 'May Allah have mercy on you and send blessings upon you,' and he did not descend into his grave, and said: 'This is how the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did with Ibrahim (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do when visiting his son Ibrahim's grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the jurisprudential precedent for visiting graves by recording Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib’s (peace be upon him) visit to his son Ismail’s grave, where he recited supplications without descending into the grave. It explicitly links this practice to the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) visit to his son Ibrahim, thereby validating the custom of standing by the grave for prayer rather than entering it, a distinction often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the etiquette of *Ziyarat al-Qubur*.
